role.altitude: The nuclear engineer keeps directing work, reviewing designs and work packages, meeting regulators, walking down procedures and deciding corrective actions; compiling status sheets, maintaining traceability spreadsheets, chasing actions by mail and copying setpoints shrink.
skills_to_grow: Structured procedure authoring with equipment data
role.ambitious_version: An engineer whose time goes to safety judgement, not to keeping lists in step.

tasks.short: Compile work order status, review plant status, lead the daily meeting, direct operating or maintenance activities of nuclear power plants, review work packages for safety conformity, log actions and approve completed work.

steps.what: Engineer compiles work order status and schedule into a spreadsheet for the daily meeting
Engineer reviews plant status and limiting conditions
Engineer leads the daily operations and maintenance meeting
Engineer directs operating or maintenance activities in the plant
Engineer reviews work packages for conformity to safety standards
Engineer records the meeting actions with owner and due date: typed into minutes and again into mails today, entered once in the work management system after the change
Engineer checks the final actions: each says what the meeting decided, with the right owner and due date
Engineer assigns the checked actions to their owners in the work management system
Engineer approves completed work records

tasks.design: A dashboard on the work management system shows open work orders, schedule and condition timers for the daily meeting, instead of a spreadsheet compiled each morning. Meeting actions are entered once in the work management system with owner and due date, instead of typed into minutes and mailed. Reviewing status, leading the meeting, directing work, reviewing packages and approving work stay with the engineer.

approvals.approved_version: The meeting actions with owners and due dates exactly as checked by the engineer in s6b, assigned once to those owners in the work management system; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Status was compiled into spreadsheets and actions were mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards on the work management system and action tracking.
tasks.still_hard: Outage periods with thousands of parallel work orders.
tasks.human_edge: Holding a job back because the plant state does not feel right.

reach.learn: Whether actions reach them on the day.

evidence.claim: AI used as a safety component in the supply of electricity is high-risk; this design uses dashboards and records only.

assumptions: Boundary: directing operations and maintenance; monitoring operations for safety violations (task 5380) and ordering shutdowns (task 5385) are sibling tasks.
s1 saves compiling status already in the work management system; s6 saves typing actions twice and keeps 55 for writing them once; checking and assigning the actions keep their full time.
Status review, the meeting, directing, reviewing and approving keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of time in outage periods.

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the dashboard filters current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: in outage periods the dashboard cannot follow the volume of work orders, so the engineer still compiles part of the status and s1 keeps 60 (4.0); high: steady operation, s1 keeps 30 (5.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define requirements, design systems and run analyses, review contractor designs, check requirement coverage, attend design reviews, track contractor deliverables and inspect on site to design or oversee construction or operation of nuclear reactors, power plants or fuel systems.

steps.what: Engineer defines design requirements and safety criteria
Engineer designs systems for nuclear reactors or power plants and runs analyses
Engineer reviews contractor design documents and drawings
Engineer checks the final review comments before release: each comment says what is wrong against which requirement, and it goes to the right contractor document
Engineer releases the checked review comments to the contractor in the comment register
Engineer links each requirement to the design documents that meet it and checks coverage: in a spreadsheet today, in the requirements tool that shows gaps after the change
Engineer attends design reviews and construction meetings
Engineer tracks contractor deliverables and comment responses by mail
Engineer oversees construction or operation on site

tasks.design: A requirements tool holds each requirement with links to the design documents, analyses and tests that meet it, and shows gaps, instead of a traceability spreadsheet updated by hand. Contractor deliverables go through document control with a review workflow and a comment register that both sides see, instead of mail. Defining requirements, designing, reviewing, design reviews and site oversight stay with the engineer.

approvals.approved_version: The review comments on the named contractor document revision exactly as checked by the engineer in s3b, released once to that contractor in the comment register; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Traceability and contractor comments lived in spreadsheets and mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Requirements tools with traceability and document control with comment registers.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy plant documents without requirement identifiers.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a design meets the letter of a requirement but not its intent.
tasks.altitude: Less list keeping; design judgement stays.

evidence.claim: A requirements and verification tool without AI is used by a grid operator and government.

assumptions: Boundary: designing and overseeing plants; designing nuclear equipment (task 5384) and discussing proposals with vendors and review boards (task 20959) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s6: contractors deliver through document control on about 60% of projects; s6 is priced at that share.

s4 keeps 70: the engineer still sets every link and checks each coverage claim; the tool removes searching the sheet for gaps and carrying links to new revisions. No separate new work is counted for keeping links current.
Defining, designing, reviewing, meetings and site work keep their full time.
research_questions: Are coverage gaps found earlier in design?

incremental.description: No new work: keeping requirement links current at each revision is the work of s4 and stays in its remaining time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: legacy plant documents lack requirement identifiers, so linking (s4) keeps 90, and contractors use document control on only 30% of projects, so tracking (s6) keeps 75 (2.4); high: 60% coverage as assumed (5.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track permit conditions and deadlines, check monitoring results against limits, direct environmental compliance activities associated with nuclear plant operations, review work for compliance, meet regulators, chase open actions and decide corrective actions.

steps.what: Engineer tracks permit conditions and deadlines in a spreadsheet
Engineer checks effluent and emission monitoring results against permit limits
Engineer directs staff on environmental compliance activities
Engineer reviews procedures and maintenance work for environmental compliance
Engineer meets regulators and inspectors
Engineer chases owners of open compliance actions by mail
Engineer decides corrective actions for deviations

tasks.design: A compliance register holds each permit condition with its deadline, owner and evidence, and sends reminders to owners of open actions, instead of a spreadsheet and mails. A dashboard on the monitoring data compares effluent and emission results with permit limits and flags any approach to a limit. Directing staff, reviewing work, meeting regulators and deciding corrective actions stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Obligations lived in spreadsheets and results were compared with limits by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Compliance registers with reminders and limit dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Permit conditions written as open norms.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a deviation to an inspector so trust is kept.
tasks.altitude: Less list keeping; compliance judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether deadlines are met without reminders.

evidence.claim: Recurring status reports become a dashboard, and deadline tracking a records app.

assumptions: Boundary: directing environmental compliance; preparing environmental impact statements and reports to agencies (task 19643) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: about 70% of monitoring points feed the plant data system; s2 is priced at that share.
s1 and s6 save keeping and chasing lists by hand; s1 keeps 40 for entering new or changed permit conditions and reading reminders, so no separate new work is counted.
Directing, reviewing, meeting and deciding keep their full time.
research_questions: Are compliance deadlines missed less often?

incremental.description: No new work: entering new or changed permit conditions is part of s1 and stays in its remaining time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only 40% of monitoring points feed the plant data system, so checking results (s2) keeps 75 (8.9); high: about 70% feed it as assumed (10.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather design data, write operational instructions for nuclear plant operation or fuel or waste handling, check setpoints and references, walk down the instruction, discuss comments, revise, have it independently approved and issue it.

steps.what: Engineer copies equipment tags, setpoints and references from drawings and datasheets
Engineer writes the operational instructions step by step
Engineer checks setpoints and references against the design documents
Engineer walks down the instruction in the plant with operators
Engineer discusses comments with operators and reviewers
Engineer revises the instruction
Independent reviewer checks the final instruction against the design basis and walkdown findings, and approves it for issue to the operating crews
Engineer issues the approved instruction in document control

tasks.design: Instructions are written in a structured authoring tool that enforces the plant's writer's guide and offers a library of standard steps, such as isolations and verifications. Equipment tags, setpoints and references come from the plant equipment database instead of being copied from drawings. A check confirms that every tag and setpoint matches the database and every reference is the current revision. No model writes or edits instruction text, because a changed procedure is a safety change. Walkdowns, comment resolution, revision and independent approval stay with people.

approvals.approved_version: The instruction at the revision approved by the independent reviewer in s7, issued once in document control to the operating crews' procedure set; any change needs a new review and revision.

tasks.previous_blocker: Tags and setpoints were copied by hand and checked line by line.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured procedure authoring linked to the equipment database.
tasks.still_hard: Older systems missing from the equipment database.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a step so a tired operator cannot misread it at night.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and checking; the instruction craft stays.

evidence.claim: At 27 sites a pharmaceutical maker cut validation cycle time by more than 50% with paperless validation documents; vendor case.
Documents suit an artefact generator; here the generated parts are data fields, not text.

assumptions: Boundary: writing operational instructions; preparing technical reports (task 20956) and recommending preventive measures (task 5386) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1 and s3: equipment and setpoints held in the plant equipment database for about 70% of systems; s1 and s3 are priced at that share.
s2 is priced low: the step library and enforced format save layout and repeated steps; the engineer writes every instruction.
Independent reviewer time is shown in s7 and does not change.
unknowns: Number of instructions revised per year.
research_questions: Do walkdowns find fewer tag and setpoint errors?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the step library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the equipment database holds only 40% of systems, so copying tags (s1) keeps 77 and checking setpoints (s3) keeps 72 (13.2); high: about 70% of systems held as assumed (17.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
